profile.headline: Software Engineer at NVIDIA
profile.summary:
I'm Guillermo "Memo" Gonzalez, a first-generation student from Ontario, California. I studied Computer Science at Berkeley with an interest in understanding computer security and privacy, and communication networks.
I support my Latinx community by providing them resources and connections, mentoring and advice, and a place of home and community.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
2.5 years Python developer for NGC 
1.5 years backend developer for NGC

company.name: UC Berkeley Hispanic Engineers and Scientists

positions.title: Treasurer for Hispanic Engineers and Scientists
positions.description:
I proudly served as the Treasurer board member in HES. 
I consistently maintained the expenses and incomes to continuously update our budget, assisted other board members in planning and executing their events to allow for maximum effect with minimum cost, hosted meeting presentations with the President and Vice President to speak with companies, and ultimately gave my as much of my assistance to all board members and HES as a whole.

positions.title: Web Design Lead Instructor
positions.description:
•	I taught a diverse group of students a project-based coding course that covered the fundamentals of HTML, CSS, and Design Thinking practices. This required me to create an inclusive and casual classroom based on the values of Social Justice, Community, Accountability, Smart Risks, and Love.
•	I ensured students developed sufficient understanding to build their own website. 
•	Over the 6 weeks, I learned how to effectively speak, present, and teach, answer questions in a clear and helpful way, lead a virtual class of 9 students to focus on teamwork, respect, and support, and made suggestions and improvements to the course material. 
•      Linked are my students' final projects!!

positions.title: Research Assistant for SDK Classification
positions.description: I worked on developing a classifier for phone application SDK's. Many phone applications uses SDK's, yet SDK's aren't regulated or checked. By looking at incoming and outgoing traffic collected from phone applications, we categorize each traffic to SDK Name, version number, and SDK type. This will make it easier to analyze SDK's and identify whether sensitive information is being transmitted. Currently in progress of finishing.

company.name: BLUES (The Berkeley Laboratory for Usable and Experimental Security) Lab @ Berkeley

positions.title: Research Assistant for Computational Modeling of Child Language
positions.description: I worked on developing a web tool that will allow people to annotate the meanings of each word in a sentence. Pulling child speech from CHILDES-DB, we loaded sentences onto the webpage which users would annotate each context word to a specific part of speech. This would eventually be made to collect data and automate the process of annotating.

company.name: LCD ( Language and Cognitive Development ) Lab @ Berkeley

positions.title: Key Club President
positions.description:
I proudly served as the president for Key Club at my high school in Division 15, Region 13.
During that time, I helped increase membership by 50% and thus increased our presence among other Key Club events in our district. As the club hung by a thread in my high school, I helped bring back its life and influenced younger members to continuously participate. 
I also received the D15 Distinguished Giraffe Award for my high DCM attendance and great involvement.

positions.title: Student
positions.description:
I joined this program for the summer for learn about market discovery-methods for data collection over 4 weeks to deliver data-driven apps. I learned HTML, CSS, and JQuery in order to build a website.
My partner and I developed a website aimed to helping students. We created website with a calendar, motivational quotes, alerts and reminders, a timer, and a mechanism to block out any other apps that are distracting. We won first place as the best idea, design, and implementation.

courses.name: CS61A (The Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs)

honors.title: Cal NERDS 2019 NSF LSAMP Research Scholar
honors.description: CAL Nerds was able to fund me to do research over the summer, partake in their workshops and info-sessions all about graduate school, and funded me to attend the SACNAS 2019 Conference.

honors.title: HES Service Award
honors.description: I received the Service Award from HES for being the member who completed the most volunteering hours in general meeting events, fundraisers, and the board as a whole.
honors.issuer: Issued by Hispanic Engineers and Scientists · May 2019

projects.title: Acoustic Positioning System Lab
projects.description:
Made an acoustic position system and understood the mathematical tools used for
shifting and detecting signals

projects.title: Simulation of Wi-Fi Protocols
projects.description:
We developed a flexible model via Python code to gain insights on how different WiFi protocols in the 802.11 family work out according to our proposed metrics.
Developed classes for Packets, Protocols Devices, and the Channel in order to simulate the throughput, collisions, interference, and successful transmission.
Applied previous coding experience with a personally-new topic to implement an actual program that simulates the written protocol into real life!

organizations.name: Hispanic Engineers and Scientists
organizations.description:
I held the Treasurer Board Member Position from May 2019 until May 2020.
Currently I am the President since May 2020.
